classification.difficultyReason: Express the four unshaded triangle areas in terms of one length, form a quadratic and check both roots against the geometry.

content.prompt: In the diagram below, $ABCD$ is a rectangle in which $AB=16\text{ cm}$ and $BC=12\text{ cm}$ and $AP=BQ=CR=DS$. The area of the shaded figure $PQRS$ is $112\text{ cm}^2$. Find the length of $AP$.

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 11, rectangle beneath the stem
spec.description: Rectangle ABCD with P, Q, R and S on successive sides, all eight labels, double ticks on AP, BQ, CR and DS, and shaded interior PQRS. Ordinary edges and marks use black; the area-defining shading uses house light blue.
spec.mathematics: AB=16 cm, BC=12 cm and AP=BQ=CR=DS. Shading identifies the quadrilateral of area 112 cm². Drawing coordinates are illustrative and introduce no additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels, equal-length marks and region shading are permanent question content.

answer.short:
$AP=4\text{ cm}$ or $10\text{ cm}$.

Subtract the four corner triangles from the rectangle and solve the resulting quadratic; both lengths satisfy the stated conditions.
answer.worked:
Let $AP=BQ=CR=DS=x$ cm, where $0<x<12$. Then $PB=DR=16-x$ and $AS=CQ=12-x$.

The four corner triangles have total area
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{corners}}&=2\left(\frac12x(16-x)\right)+2\left(\frac12x(12-x)\right)\\A_{\text{corners}}&=28x-2x^2.\end{align*}$$

Subtract these areas from the rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}16\times12-(28x-2x^2)&=112\\2x^2-28x+80&=0\\x^2-14x+40&=0\\(x-4)(x-10)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }x=10.\end{align*}$$

Both roots lie between $0$ and $12$. For either root, the corner areas total $80\text{ cm}^2$, leaving $192-80=112\text{ cm}^2$. Hence $AP=4\text{ cm}$ or $10\text{ cm}$.
